paper.citation: Wager, S. and Athey, S. (2018). Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523), 1228-1242. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.2017.1319839.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_locator: Section 5.1 'Experimental Setup', arXiv:1510.04342v4 (10 Jul 2017) PDF p.20, equation (27); the sentence 'We used n = 500 samples and varied d between 2 and 30' follows the equation on the same page.

mechanism.name: Wager–Athey (2018) simulation 1: zero treatment effect with a beta-density propensity

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = m(X) + A tau(X) + eps, eps ~ Normal(0,1)

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference between individuals
Unconfoundedness: {Y(0), Y(1)} independent of A given X. In the source this is enforced by construction because the outcome depends on X only through m(X) and the effect is constant
Overlap: 0.25 <= e(X) <= 0.777 on the whole support of X, since 20 u (1-u)^3 attains its maximum 2.109 at u = 0.25
Homoscedastic Gaussian noise with unit variance, as in the source

properties.notes: Five ambient covariates but only X1 is active, so effective dimension is 1. Nonlinearity comes from the quartic beta-density propensity, not from the effect surface, which is constant. No interaction term.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query point; in this design it is identically zero for every x, which makes it a null-effect control for bias and interval coverage under confounding.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query point; in this design it is identically zero for every x, which makes it a null-effect control for bias and interval coverage under confounding.
truth.derivation: Closed form: the declared surface is identically zero, so the population CATE is exactly 0 at every query point; verified against the realised outcome column.

adaptations: Dimension is fixed at d = 5 instead of the source's d in {2,...,30}; only X1 enters the propensity and the baseline, X2-X5 are irrelevant coordinates kept so the design still has ambient dimension.

The source writes Y = m(X) + (W - 0.5) tau(X) + eps; this package uses the equivalent contrast form Y = m(X) + A tau(X) + eps with A in {0,1}. The CATE is unchanged, the marginal outcome law differs by the constant 0.5 tau(X) = 0.
The source reports MSE and coverage over 500 replications at n = 500; this package fixes one scenario and is checked at n = 128 for interface purposes only. No estimator is re-run.
beta_{2,4} is the Beta(2,4) *density* in the source; it is implemented as 20 u (1-u)^3 so that e(X) = 0.25 (1 + 20 X1 (1-X1)^3).
